title: arXiv Mathematics — Friday, 6 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred reading order, not a popularity ranking. The papers are very recent, citation evidence is immature, and only one selected paper yielded an independent quantitative attention signal.

sections.title: Quadratic Extractors
sections.abstract: For quadratic sources over F_2^n, the authors give an explicit extractor whose min-entropy requirement is polylogarithmic in n, far below the previous roughly n-sqrt(log n) requirement.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.3 gives an explicit extractor for quadratic sources at min-entropy at least log^C n, with error n^-Omega(1); the authors describe it as the first construction beyond the sumset-extractor barrier.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The source is the image of hidden uniform bits under a map of n quadratic polynomials over F_2; this is a structured-source result, not an extractor for arbitrary weak sources.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is limited to quadratic sources and does not remove the impossibility for unrestricted weak sources.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A parameter breakthrough across complexity, cryptography, and combinatorics. Independent ECCC report TR26-303 displayed 146 downloads when checked; this is an ECCC report count, not arXiv downloads or citations.

sections.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
sections.abstract: The authors prove that a K3 surface without an F_q-rational point exists exactly when q<=11, using lattice bounds, the Artin-Tate formula, and Niemeier-lattice embeddings.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1 proves existence of pointless K3 surfaces over F_q if and only if q<=11.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth K3 surfaces over finite fields; the statement concerns existence of at least one surface for each field size.
sections.unique_caveat: The proof uses numerical computations, with code and data linked by the authors; they note an independent proof and leave the relation between approaches unexplored.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A sharp iff cutoff across arithmetic geometry and number theory, with a stated downstream improvement to a rational-point bound for threefold results.

sections.title: Resolving Tusnády's Problem
sections.abstract: The paper proves the missing higher-dimensional lower bound for combinatorial discrepancy of axis-parallel boxes, which with the known upper bound and planar result gives the sharp order in every fixed dimension d>=2.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 gives Omega_d((log N)^(d-1/2)) for anchored-box discrepancy for fixed d>=3; with Nikolov's upper bound and Wei's planar result, the authors conclude Theta_d((log N)^(d-1/2)) for boxes for every fixed d>=2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Worst-case discrepancy of finite N-point sets, with dimension fixed as N grows; constants and threshold may depend on dimension.
sections.unique_caveat: The new lower-bound theorem is for fixed d>=3; constants are not optimized or uniform in dimension, and the full conclusion uses prior upper and planar bounds.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors claim to close a longstanding logarithmic-factor gap; the paper is cross-listed in analysis, computational geometry, algorithms, and combinatorics.

sections.title: Tusnády's problem and online two-sample thinning
sections.abstract: The paper proves the sharp fixed-dimensional Tusnády discrepancy order, a robust random-sample lower bound, and minimax rates for online thinning of two samples from an unknown common distribution.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed dimension k and expected deletion budget rho*n, 0<rho<2, the authors obtain minimax expected prefix discrepancy Theta_(k,rho)((log n)^(k+1/2)); in one dimension the optimal terminal rate is Theta_rho((log log n)^(3/2)).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two independent size-n samples from the same unknown distribution; keep/discard decisions are online and irrevocable.
sections.unique_caveat: For k>=2, terminal upper and lower bounds differ by a factor log n. Its sharp Tusnády theorem also appears independently in paper 3 of this batch.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across discrepancy, algorithms, and probability; it adds online prefix and terminal guarantees under a deletion budget to the sharp-box result.

sections.title: Rational Turán exponents of a single k-uniform hypergraph
sections.abstract: For every integer k>=2 and rational r in [0,1], the authors construct a single forbidden k-uniform hypergraph with extremal number of order n^(k-r), and give an obstruction for part of the larger-exponent range.
sections.claimed_result: For rational r in [0,1], there is F_(k,r) with ex_k(n,F_(k,r))=Theta(n^(k-r)); for k>=4 and ceil(k/2)<r<=k-1, a single-F realization is impossible.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Fixed uniformity k, rational exponent, and the standard extremal number for avoiding one finite hypergraph.
sections.unique_caveat: The Lean 4 formalization is conditional on two stated axioms; positive realization is shown for r in [0,1], with nonexistence proved only on the stated higher range.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Extends rational-exponent realization from graphs to uniform hypergraphs in the single-forbidden-object setting, with linked formalization.

sections.title: Weak uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate diffusion: the full Hölder regime
sections.abstract: For scalar stochastic heat equations on the one-dimensional torus, the authors prove weak well-posedness for uniformly nondegenerate diffusion coefficients of every positive Hölder order and extend results to measurable drifts of linear growth.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 proves existence and uniqueness in law for bounded, uniformly nondegenerate Hölder diffusion at every exponent beta>0; Theorem 1.2 treats measurable linear-growth drifts and certain unbounded diffusions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Scalar equation driven by space-time white noise on the one-dimensional torus; the main theorem assumes deterministic L2 initial data and diffusion bounded above and away from zero.
sections.unique_caveat: This is weak uniqueness, not pathwise uniqueness; the stated unbounded-diffusion extension uses bounded initial data.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Closes the positive-Hölder range left by the author's earlier result and links a Lean formalization.

sections.title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
sections.abstract: Every complete noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded constant-mean-curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is shown to be minimal, in every dimension.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves that a complete, noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded CMC hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space has zero mean curvature.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Euclidean ambient space of arbitrary dimension; completeness, noncompactness, two-sidedness, proper embeddedness, and finite Morse index are required.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is for properly embedded hypersurfaces, not general immersed or non-proper hypersurfaces.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A claimed all-dimensions resolution of the properly embedded finite-index case without curvature or volume-growth bounds; cross-listed in geometry and PDE.

sections.title: Gelfand numbers of Schatten class embeddings in the quasi-Banach range
sections.abstract: The paper proves a 2022 conjectured lower bound for finite-dimensional Schatten-class embeddings when 0<p<=1, yielding exact asymptotic orders in the previously unresolved range.
sections.claimed_result: Proves Conjecture 1.4 of Prochno and Strzelecki for indices proportionally separated from ambient dimension, uniformly for 2<=q<=infinity; with known upper estimates this yields the exact order.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Gelfand numbers of embeddings between finite-dimensional Schatten classes in the quasi-Banach range 0<p<=1, target exponent q>=2.
sections.unique_caveat: The new lower bound has the stated proportional separation from ambient dimension; the all-index conclusion combines prior estimates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Resolves a named conjecture and completes the all-index asymptotic description together with earlier upper estimates.

sections.title: Exotic smooth structures on complex projective spaces
sections.abstract: The authors give evidence for the conjecture that every CP^n, n>3, admits an exotic smooth structure: the dimensions with such structures have natural density one, and 266 residue classes modulo 288 are covered.
sections.claimed_result: Proves density one of complex dimensions admitting an exotic smooth structure and identifies 266 congruence classes modulo 288, covering more than 92% of dimensions n>3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth structures on the topological manifold underlying complex projective space for n>3; proof uses stable cohomotopy and height-two chromatic computations.
sections.unique_caveat: The conjecture for every dimension n>3 remains open; density one and the listed residue classes do not settle exceptional dimensions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A density-one theorem and large explicit congruence-class construction give a quantified partial classification.

sections.title: Two-row Schur times Schubert via parallel classes of positroid varieties
sections.abstract: The author gives a positive combinatorial formula for Schubert structure constants when one indexing partition has two rows, using increasing chains and parallel classes of positroid varieties.
sections.claimed_result: The paper expresses the relevant two-row coefficients through Kostka numbers and combinatorial data from increasing chains and positroid parallel classes.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Schubert structure constants for complete flag varieties, with the second partition index restricted to two rows.
sections.unique_caveat: The result addresses the two-row case, not a general positive formula for arbitrary indexing partitions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Resolves a specifically identified next case in positive Schubert-calculus formulas and is cross-listed in combinatorics and algebraic geometry.

sections.title: Bergman Kernel Zeros on Rational Hartogs Triangles
sections.abstract: For relatively prime positive integers m>n, the authors prove the Edholm-Mathew polynomial nonvanishing conjecture and characterize exactly when the associated rational Hartogs triangle has a zero-free Bergman kernel.
sections.claimed_result: Proves strict positivity of the associated trigonometric polynomial, deduces exactly m-n zeros in the punctured unit disc, and shows the Hartogs triangle has zero-free Bergman kernel precisely when its exponent is a reciprocal of a positive integer.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Rational Hartogs triangles parameterized by relatively prime positive integers m>n; zeros are counted with multiplicity.
sections.unique_caveat: The criterion is for this rational family and does not establish a classification for more general domains.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Resolves a named conjecture with a positivity bound and an iff classification for the rational family.

sections.title: An Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method for Bures-Wasserstein Space
sections.abstract: By lifting suitable composite optimization problems on Bures-Wasserstein space to Euclidean affine-transport maps, the authors obtain an accelerated method with O(k^-2) objective-gap rate.
sections.claimed_result: Under convex smooth/proximable affine-lift assumptions, BW-FISTA achieves O(k^-2); for Gaussian variational inference with a log-concave, log-smooth target, the authors improve the stated rate from O(k^-1) to O(k^-2).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Composite optimization over Gaussian measures in Bures-Wasserstein space with convexity and affine-lift regularity; the variational-inference application assumes a log-concave, log-smooth target.
sections.unique_caveat: The guarantees depend on the stated lift and regularity conditions; numerical experiments reported in the abstract are synthetic.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv comment reports acceptance to a NeurIPS 2026 workshop; the paper states a minimax-optimal rate for a defined class and an improved Gaussian variational-inference rate.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
text: Two independent papers in the same batch state the sharp fixed-dimensional Tusnady discrepancy order; one extends to robust random samples and online thinning, using a different proof route.
The quadratic-extractor, rational-Turan, and exotic-CP^n papers give explicit parameter thresholds in different mathematical settings, not a shared technique.

The stochastic-heat and Turan papers link Lean formalizations (the latter conditional on two axioms); the K3 paper supplies numerical code/data. These are distinct proof artifacts, not interchangeable certification guarantees.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
text: Author-stated gap: online terminal discrepancy bounds for dimension k>=2 differ by log n; seek a matching algorithm or lower bound. [2611.08455]
Author-stated conjecture: every CP^n, n>3, admits an exotic smooth structure; uncovered residue classes remain. [2611.08406]
Author-stated discussion: the K3 paper leaves unexplained the apparent relation between its Artin-Tate/lattice argument and an independent proof. [2611.08356]
Author-stated boundary: single-hypergraph Turan exponents are realized for r in [0,1], while impossibility is shown for k>=4 and ceil(k/2)<r<=k-1; remaining ranges can be tested. [2611.07290]
Synthesis: test whether the two-row Schubert formula extends to three-row partitions. [2611.07351]

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: This batch's strongest stories are claimed sharp discrepancy bounds, a q=11 cutoff for pointless K3 surfaces, and major parameter refinements for structured extraction and hypergraph extremal numbers. Ordering is an inferred shortlist, not measured popularity; recent-paper citation evidence is immature and the preprints need expert review.
